items.title: How KPMG Closed the Design-to-Engineering Gap with Builder
items.excerpt: KPMG adopted Builder's AI design-intelligence system to close the design-to-engineering gap, cutting delivery time 88% by driving component-based code generation with explicit architectural rules instead of probabilistic pattern inference. Design review cycles dropped from 10 days to same-day turnaround.

items.title: The crisis of the what: AI took the how. Now it's coming for the what
items.excerpt: UX Collective essay arguing that AI has already absorbed the 'how' of design execution and is now moving on the 'what' — the framing and problem-definition work designers considered safe — and what that means for the discipline's next role.

items.title: Otoy releases OctaneRender 2026.4
items.excerpt: Otoy's GPU renderer update expands the Neural Radiance Cache — a neural network trained at render time to cut noise in indirectly lit scenes — to macOS and network rendering, and extends 3D Gaussian Splatting support.

items.title: Reallusion releases Headshot 3.1
items.excerpt: Reallusion updated its AI head-generation plugin for Character Creator with new texture-editing tools and integrated Google Nano Banana image generation, so 3D digital doubles from reference photos can be refined without leaving the software.

items.title: New Free Tool Automatically Creates Clean Quad Topology (AutoRemesher 1.0)
items.excerpt: AutoRemesher hit 1.0: a free, MIT-licensed retopology tool that converts high-poly meshes into clean quad topology, landing amid a surge of AI-powered retopo tools like Tractive and CozyBlanket Pro. Note: the tool itself is algorithmic; AI angle is contextual.

items.title: Rolls-Royce — wrestling back control
items.excerpt: Rolls-Royce is ditching heavily customised PLM for out-of-the-box cloud software and low-code tools to open its engineering data up to AI — pairing Siemens Intelligence Center X with internal data lakes so teams surface their own insights at the point problems emerge.

items.title: nTop and CoreWeave tackle NASA's Vision 2030 with time to spare
items.excerpt: nTop and CoreWeave ran 12,000 CFD simulations across 2,400 drone geometry variants lights-out, without manual intervention — a dataset the team says is viable for training AI surrogate models that predict aerodynamic performance without re-running simulation.

items.title: Get Ready For the Powerful CSS border-shape Property!
items.excerpt: Temani Afif previews the upcoming CSS border-shape property, a major new shape-creation capability for design engineers. Note: fresh design-craft shift but no direct AI angle — weakest-tier candidate; no fresher AI item surfaced from tokens sources this window.

items.title: 18Birdies & Arccos Make Meta Glasses Act As Your AI Golf Caddy
items.excerpt: Meta integrated the 18Birdies and Arccos golf apps into its AI smart glasses, letting wearers query a voice-driven virtual caddy — an example of third-party AI experiences designed for the glasses form factor, live now in the US and Canada.

items.title: VR Design Unpacked: Why 'Embodiment' is More Important Than 'Immersion'
items.excerpt: Road to VR's design column argues embodiment — how players physically inhabit and act in a virtual world — matters more than attention-based immersion, using Synapse as a case study. Note: XR design craft piece with no direct AI angle.

items.title: SimX adds AI Assistant to healthcare VR training
items.excerpt: SimX launched an AI Assistant that automates patient and care-team characters in room-scale VR medical training scenarios — expert-authored rather than open-ended generative AI — letting educators scale multi-learner simulations without extra staff. (Domain is on the cad allowed list; topic is VR.)

items.title: OpenAI gets permission to roll out GPT-5.6 to the public on July 9
items.excerpt: OpenAI will publicly launch all three GPT-5.6 variants — Sol, Luna and Terra — on July 9 after US government approval, expanding preview access globally. A frontier-model release that will land directly in designers' daily AI tooling.

items.title: ChatGPT's new voice mode will slow down if you tell it to
items.excerpt: OpenAI released GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1 mini, duplex voice models that process input while speaking for more natural conversations — pausing when you think and slowing down on request. A notable shift for voice/multimodal interface design.

items.title: How AI is challenging traditional business categories and creating new paths for growth and innovation
items.excerpt: Profile of creative accelerator Piranha on how AI is dissolving category lines in creative services — research cited says skills are changing 116% faster in AI-exposed occupations, reshaping what design and branding teams are hired to do.

items.title: Skill issue: how we built an OS for PMs at Figma | Config 2026
items.excerpt: Config 2026 session video: how Figma's team packaged agent Skills into an internal 'operating system' for PMs — a concrete playbook for encoding team workflows into AI agents.

items.title: Designing money: how to build a trustworthy brand in the age of AI ft. Chris Warner | Config 2026
items.excerpt: Config 2026 session video with Chris Warner on building trustworthy fintech brands in the AI era — how brand designers establish credibility when AI-generated polish is everywhere.

items.title: Easy AI VFX You Can Add to Any Video
items.excerpt: Matt Wolfe walks through adding AI visual effects to any video without making everything look AI-generated — the workflow behind the intros of his weekly AI news videos.
